lines: TO: Honorable Mayor and City Council
THROUGH: Housing, Homelessness and Planning Committee (June 3, 2026)
SUBJECT: PUBLIC HEARING: APPROVAL OF THE ANNUAL ACTION PLAN
(2026) AND RELATED FUNDING APPLICATIONS FOR THE
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT, HOME INVESTMENT
PARTNERSHIP ACT, AND EMERGENCY SOLUTIONS GRANT
It is recommended that upon close of the public hearing the City Council take the following
1. Find that the recommended actions are not a "project" subject to the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Public Resources Code Section
21065 and within the meaning of State CEQA Guidelines Section 15378(b)(4)
2. Approve the submittal of a grant application for CDBG Program Year 2026
entitlement funds in the amount of $2,164,886, and the reprogramming of
existing unspent CDBG funds in the amount of $912,114 for a total of $3,077,000
to be allocated towards CDBG program activities;
3. Approve the submittal of a grant application for hlOME Program Year 2026
entitlement funds in the amount of $662,156 to be allocated towards HOME
4. Approve the submittal of a grant application for ESG Program Year 2026
entitlement funds in the amount of $188,739, $290,365 in unspent prior year ESG
funds, and the reprogramming of existing unspent Rapid Unsheltered Survivor
Housing (RUSH) disaster grant funding in the amount of $470,136 for a total of
$949,240 to be allocated towards ESG program activities; and
5. Authorize the City Manager to execute, and the City Clerk to attest, the Annual
Action Plan (2026), the grant applications, administrative amendments (such as
time extensions, policy revisions, and budget modification corrections),
certifications, and any and all other documents deemed necessary by hlUD to
obtain the allocation of the aforementioned federal entitlement funds.
The Annual Action Plan sets forth the projected use of funds for the coming program
year and addresses the available resources for program implementation, activities to be
undertaken, program guidelines, and monitoring. The Action Plan identifies efforts to be
made toward accomplishing the goals and objectives included in the City's Five-Year
Consolidated Plan. The draft 2026 Annual Action Plan (Attachment B) was available for
public review and comment from April 16 through May 15, 2026. Any comments
received will be included in the final version prior to submission HDD. Recommended
funding allocations under the CDBG, HOME, and ESQ programs are summarized in

Table two summarizes the proposed goals and funding to address community needs

This proposed action supports the City Council's strategic goals in the areas of
improving, maintaining, and enhancing public facilities and infrastructure; improving
mobility and accessibility throughout the City of Pasadena; and supporting and
promoting the quality of life and the local economy.
CEQA excludes, from environmental review, actions that are not "projects" as defined
by Public Resources Code Section 21065 and within the meaning of State CEQA
Guidelines Section 15378(b). Sections 21065 and 15378(b) define a project as an
action which may cause either a direct physical change in the environment, or a
reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. Section
15378(b)(4) and (5) excludes from the definition of "project" government fiscal activities
which do not involve any commitment to any specific project which may result in a
potentially significant physical impact on the environment or administrative activities of
governments that will not result in direct or indirect physical changes in the environment.
The recommended actions will have no direct fiscal impact. City Council approval of the
Plan and grant application submissions, and subsequent approval thereof by HUD, will
result in a total allocation to the City of $4,688,396 in CDBG, ESG and HOME funds to
support housing, community development, and homeless prevention activities. These
federal funds wilt be included as revenue in the proposed FY 2027 operating budget of
the Housing Department. Approval also enables the City to be eligible for other
federally funded programs that are consistent with an adopted Five-Year Consolidated
